questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is correctly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word.**

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

They were quite

A- I was fluent in English

B- fascinated, and were quick to

C- remark that they were surprised
questions.solution:
The correct option will be **BCA.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **‘They were quite’** is in the past tense. So, the verb that follows should be in the past tense **'**fascinated'.
 
• This implies part B should be the first in the sequence.
 
• Also, the*** verb*** that follows is in simple present. So, the next part of the sequence is **C**.
 
• Part **A** forms a suitable ending of the sentence.
 
• ***They were quite fascinated and were quick to remark that they were surprised I was fluent in English. ***This will be the correct order of the sentence, as this gives proper meaning to the sentence.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is BCA, making **option 3** the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “no improvement”.**

She thought she (have rediscovered) her real self after a long time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **had rediscovered.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• ** **Every sentence follows the rule of tense consistency**. **
 
• The first part of the sentence is in the simple past tense (She thought). So, the next action that we talk about should be in **Past Perfect tense (had + verb³ ).**
 
• Examples-
 
 
• *I found that I had forgotten the formula.*
 
• *Indian team won the test match as all the players had contributed in the field. *

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “no improvement”.**

A neem tree grew as a bonus on the side, raising its head high as if it wants (will peep) into my bedroom.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer** is **'To peep'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **To Peep** means to **secretly look at something**.
 
• '**wants will peep’** is not grammatically correct and hence, the sentence needs an improvement.
 
• The correct phrase we are looking for is** *to peep.* **
 
• The verb that follows ***wants** *should use the preposition** *****to** *(examples: *wants to eat, wants to sleep, wants to dance,* etc.)

***Correct sentence__*** - *A neem tree grew as a bonus on the side, raising its head high as if it wants **to peep** into my bedroom.*

Thus, the correct answer is **option ****3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The **to-infinitive** can be used to express purpose or necessity after a verb followed by a pronoun or a noun.

*Ram wants **to** play cricket all day long. *

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.

Of or connected with the sense of touch
questions.solution:
**The correct answer** is **Tactile.**** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us look at the meanings of the given words:
 
 
• Apperception – the attainment of full awareness of a sensation or an idea

 
 
• **Example**: The child's apperception of mathematics concepts improved significantly after the teacher used practical examples.
 
 
 
• Eavesdrop – to listen to a private conversation secretly
 
 
• **Example**: He didn't mean to eavesdrop, but the conversation on the other side of the wall was too loud to ignore.
 
 
 
• Tactile – related or connected to the sense of touch
 
 
• **Example**: The tactile nature of clay makes it a popular medium for children learning about 3D art.
 
 
 
• Hark – to listen attentively
 
 
• **Example**: As we sat around the campfire, we would hark to the sounds of nature, becoming one with the forest around us.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• *Synonyms* of** tactile: **palpable, tactual, material, tangible, physical, solid.
 
• *Antonyms* of **tactile: **intangible, abstract, impalpable, abstract, imperceptible.

Thus, the word *tactile* expresses the desired meaning, making **option 3** the correct answer.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

She says, “I am playing tennis.”

options.text: She says that she will be playing tennis.
She said she are playing tennis.
She said she was playing tennis.
She says that she is playing tennis.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is **She says that she is playing tennis.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****

__
 
• Here the reporting verb is in the present tense, there shall be no change in the tense of reported speech, therefore the tense form of the reported speech shall be in the present tense.
 
• The preposition 'I' belongs to first person and shall change according to the Subject of the reported verb 'She'.
 
 
• 
 
 
 

 She
 says,
 "I
 am
 playing
 tennis".
 
 

 She 
 says that
 she
 is
 playing
 tennis.
 
 
 

 
 

 
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****

In Direct speech, the message is conveyed in the words of the concerned person.

In Indirect speech, the message is conveyed in our words. 

When we convert Direct speech to Indirect speech, we remove the inverted commas. Also, the conjunction *that *is added before introducing the words spoken between quotation marks (“…”). 

The point to be noted here is that if the reporting verb is in the present tense, there will be no changes to the verb in the reported speech.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Who burned the food?

options.text: By who was this food burned?
By whom was that food burned?
By whom was the food burned?
By whom is this food burned?

questions.solution:
**The correct answer **is **By whom was the food burned?**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

** __Active Voice__** – Here, the subject performs the action. There is a simple relationship between the doer of the action and the verb.

***Example:** She is eating a sandwich.*

**__Passive Voice__** - Here, the subject receives the action. More importance is given to the action (and not the subject)

***Example:** A sandwich is being eaten by her.*

Thus the correct answer is** option 3.**

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• When we want to change interrogative sentences (questions) from active to passive, we need to be aware of the following rules:
 
• The question words **how, what,** ** when, why, or where **do not change their position when these are used at the beginning of the sentence.
 
• Example :
 
 
• **Active Voice** – **What** were you taking?
 
• **Passive Voice** – **What **was being taken by you?
 
 
 
• The verbs **has, have, had, will, etc. **do not change their position when used at the beginning of the sentence.
 
• **Example :**
 
 
• **Active Voice** – **Has** she invited Rani?
 
• **Passive Voice** – **Has **Rani been invited by her?
 
 
 
• *Who *changes to *by whom *and *whom *changes to *who*
 
• Example :
 
 
• **Active Voice** – **Who** is eating the cake?
 
• **Passive Voice** – The cake is being eaten **by** **whom?**
 
 
 
• Understanding these points, we can now change the given sentence from Active to Passive Voice:
 
• **Passive Voice: *By whom was the food burned?***

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

Ever since

P : outbreaks have been an annual occurrence

Q : Indian shores during the 2009 pandemic,

R : the influenza virus H1N1 landed on
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **RQP.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Among the parts P, Q and R, the best one to be the first in the sequence is part R. ‘
 
• Ever since the influenza virus H1N1 landed on…’ seems to be logically correct.
 
• Now, the next question arises: landed where?
 
• This is answered by part Q.
 
• Part P forms the ending of the sentence.

*Ever since the influenza virus H1N1 landed on Indian shores during the 2009 pandemic, outbreaks have been an annual occurrence.*

Thus, the correct sequence is RQP, making **option 4** the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.**

Arbitrary
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Random.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arbitrary**: based on chance rather than being planned or based on reason.

 
 
• Example: For tabular presentation we used **arbitrary **cut off values.
 
 
 
• **Random: **happening, done, or chosen by chance rather than according to a plan.
 
 
• Example: I picked a CD at **random**.
 
 
 
• Thus, arbitrary and random are synonymous.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let us look into the meaning of the other words:
 
• **Methodical **– to do things in a very ordered and careful way.
 
 
• Example: The other thing he has going for him is that he is so **methodical**.
 
 
 
• **Penetrable **– allowing things to pass-through.
 
 
• Example: The one **penetrable **point in his ironclad nature had not been reached yet.
 
 
 
• **Artful **– clever or skillful.
 
 
• Example: He has shown himself to be an **artful **politician.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **option 3** as the word *random* is close in meaning.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.**

Palliate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'relieve'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The meaning of **palliate** is to reduce the severity of a disease or its symptoms.

 
 
• Example: They tried to **palliate **the hardship of their lives. 
 
 
 
• The word **relieve** means to make the disease less severe.
 
 
• Example: The drug was used to promote sleep and to **relieve **pain.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **relieve** as it **matches** the meaning of **palliate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The meaning of other words are as follows:-
 
• **Accuse** – to say that someone is responsible for a crime.
 
 
• Example: He was **accused **of stealing the money. 
 
 
 
• **Condemn** - to criticize something or someone strongly.
 
 
• Example: We strongly **condemn **this attack against our allies. 
 
 
 
• **Exacerbate** – to make a problem or a negative feeling worse.
 
 
• Example: The proposed factory shutdown would only **exacerbate **our unemployment problems.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

She must ______ a great time at her birthday party.
questions.solution:
As we have used *must* before the blank, *be * (and not *is*) should follow. Also, the verb should be in –ing form (having)

Thus, the word *be having *is the correct fit for the blank, making **option 1** the correct answer.

__Complete Sentence__ - *She must **be having** a great time at her birthday party.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

Four famous Sikh shrines in Delhi will go green (1)/by employing solar energy (2)/to meet its daily power needs from April. (3)/No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **3- the error lies in only Part 3.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

Here, the subject is *shrines *which is plural. So, instead of *its*, we should use *their *as we are referring to the daily power needs of the four Sikh shrines.

__Correct Sentence__ - *Four famous Sikh shrines in Delhi will go green by employing solar energy to meet **their** daily power needs from April.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

Cybercrime cases pose various kinds of (1)/challenges which requires strengthening of (2)/the institutional mechanism. (3)/No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **2- the error lies in part 2 only.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cybercrime cases is plural and the challenges they pose is also a plural noun. So, the verb should be in plural form also.
 
• Instead of **requires, require** should be used.
 
• Correct Sentence__ - *Cybercrime cases pose various kinds of challenges which **require** strengthening of the institutional mechanism.*

*​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

__
 
• The rule of Subject-verb agreemen__t will be followed in the sentence.
 
• Subject-verb agreement says that If a subject is singular, the verb will be singular and if the subject is plural then the verb will be plural.
 
 
• Example:-
 
 
• Nakul teaches English.(Singular subject, singular verb)
 
• A few students were missing.(plural noun, plural verb)
